newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz sees no policy change - report.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz sees no policy change - report.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said the outcome of key July 6 elections will not change the government's economic model, the Reforma reported Monday.

In an interview with the daily, Ortiz denied the elections will impact government policies. Mexicans vote for a new lower house of Congress in July and also for a mayor of Mexico City. Several governorships are also up for grabs.
"I believe that it is exactly the reverse -- whoever wins we will continue with the same policies," Ortiz said. "No change in the economic policies is seen," he added.
Ortiz said he discounted the possibility that the government planned to cobble together a contingency plan in case of market nervousness that the elections could cause.

But he recognized that the economy could be under pressure in the short term from politics. "Although politics in the short term could hit the economy, I believe the competition will be very good (for the country)...," he said.
"I am totally in disagreement with those that hold the opinion that plurality and political competition is destablizing," Ortiz added.
Ortiz criticised those worried about the exchange rate with relation to the elections. "If the market does not like it, it should move it (the exchange rate)," Ortiz said.
"The only thing we can be sure about is that markets move. In an exchange rate regime like we have, movements come in steps," Ortiz added.
